Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the invite. Quick heads up — on my calendar the invite appears as Friday, Jun 25 at 10:00 JST (not Jun 24). I think Google Calendar is showing it in my local view differently because the invite came from a US time zone. Can you confirm whether you meant Thu Jun 24 or Fri Jun 25? Both are ok for us, but we want to be sure the date is correct before accepting.

Also, Rajesh is in Singapore and I cc'd him to confirm his view.

Best,
Akiko Sato
Head of Data Partnerships
KyodoAI

On Sat, Jun 20, 2026 at 09:35 AM JST, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Akiko — thanks for flagging this.
>
> Quick explanation: when invites are created from a machine set to a US timezone (PDT/EDT) some calendar clients will convert the UTC timestamp and display the event in the recipient's locale, which can change the displayed date if the target timezone is across the date boundary. In this case the original invite was for Thu Jun 24 10:00 JST (UTC+9).
>
> To avoid any ambiguity, would Thu Jun 24 at 08:00 JST / 07:00 SGT / 09:00 AEST (45 min) work for you both? That earlier slot keeps the meeting firmly within the same calendar day for Sydney and Tokyo and avoids the overnight cutover seen in some clients.
>
> Proposed: Thu Jun 24 — 08:00 JST / 07:00 SGT / 09:00 AEST (45m)
>
> If that works I will ask Priya to send a corrected invite with explicit timezone markers ("Asia/Tokyo" / "Asia/Singapore" / "Australia/Sydney") so Google and Outlook show the same day for all participants.
>
> Cheers,
> Vivek Kulkarni
> Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
>
